- When sentiment is consistently negative (last 3–5 days), model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast downward by 1–2% of recent range.
- After sharp price spikes, model often overshoots downward in next 5–7 days; apply a “lag correction” by adding 0.5–1.5% of spike magnitude to forecast.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 50% of 30d mean), model underestimates recovery; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day until reversion.
- When sentiment is positive but price is falling, model often underreacts; add 0.3–0.7% to forecast to capture sentiment-driven rebound.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently underestimates late-period volatility; increase final 5–7 days by 0.5–1.0% if sentiment is volatile or recent price is trending.
- If sentiment history shows alternating +/– swings, model tends to “smooth” extremes; apply a “sentiment filter” to amplify 1–2% of recent sentiment magnitude in forecast direction.
